chunks: And ʿAlī ibn Jaʿfar asked his brother Mūsā ibn Jaʿfar عليهما السلام about a man whom a wild beast or birds eat, so that only his bones remain without flesh: how is he to be dealt with? He said:
He should be washed, shrouded, prayed over, and buried.

key_terms.السَّبُعُ: a wild beast that devours the body
key_terms.الطَّيْرُ: birds that consume parts of the corpse
key_terms.عِظَامُهُ: his bones remaining after the flesh is gone
key_terms.يُصَلَّى عَلَيْهِ: funeral salat is to be offered over him
key_terms.يُغَسَّلُ: he is to be given the ritual washing of the deceased
key_terms.يُكَفَّنُ: he is to be shrouded in burial cloth

ai.seo_question: What should be done if only the bones of a deceased person remain after being eaten by animals?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling concerning a deceased person whose flesh has been consumed, leaving only bones. It establishes that the funerary rites of ghusl, shrouding, funeral prayer, and burial are still to be performed.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications: Hadith.441 - Ali ibn Ja'far asked his brother Imam Musa ibn Jafar Al-Kadhim (as) about a man who has been devoured by a wild animal or birds, leaving only his bones without flesh. He asked what should be done in such a case.
Imam (as) replied: "He should be washed, shrouded, funeral prayers should be offered for him, and he should be buried”.
